collapses_to.tool: a batch form of the same keyed upsert — many findings for one source in a single request, plus the set of externalIds that should now be resolved — so a lockfile with two hundred advisories is one call rather than two hundred. Nothing about idempotency would change: the key is already documented and already server-side, so this is a throughput and rate-limit question rather than a correctness one

idempotency.verified_at: The "Idempotency/Upsert Behavior" section of https://api.noru.tech/llms.txt states that for `POST /v1/security-findings`, if `source + externalId` already exists in the organization the request returns 200 and updates the existing finding, and otherwise returns 201 and creates one. The endpoint's own "Behavior" note repeats it and documents `externalId` as "Source-native unique ID. Create is idempotent per (source, externalId)". The createSecurityFinding tool description published by https://api.noru.tech/v1/mcp says the same thing and adds that it uses the write:risks scope, matching REST.

source.note: Every finding this piece already has open in the organization. A scanner result that stopped appearing has left a finding open somewhere, and only Noru knows it is still open.
The organization's own asset inventory, so a finding attaches to an asset the register already holds, by that register's external id. This plugin ships no asset list and never creates one.

The organization's own risk register. A class of findings, or one finding, may be filed against a risk it already carries; this plugin never opens a risk and never links one that is not in the snapshot.

The treatments of a risk the manifest files findings against, read only for their due dates. A remediation deadline is whatever the organization's own treatment says; this plugin ships no remediation windows and computes none.

exit_codes.1: drift, validation failure, an expired judgement under --as-of, an input that declares it reaches a forge alert store, missing prerequisite input, or a stale plan
exit_codes.2: usage error, including a push without --confirm
